title: Tech Note: 4th Dimension, the Year 2000 and Everything
author: ACI US Technical Support

historical_commentary.text: This note reassures developers that 4D's internal Date data type stores a full four-digit year and is Year 2000-safe at the engine level, while addressing the practical UI problem of users entering only two-digit years, and presents a 'pivot year' algorithm (and the Sys date format command for detecting the OS's locale-specific date format/century-cutoff conventions) for correctly inferring the intended century from ambiguous two-digit input. The Year 2000 rollover this note anticipates has of course long since passed uneventfully for 4D-based systems, making the note's central concern historical, though the pivot-year technique for interpreting ambiguous two-digit year entry remains a conceptually valid pattern for handling legacy or intentionally-abbreviated date input in any date-parsing system today.
related_updates: The Year 2000 rollover this note prepares developers for occurred uneventfully in 2000 and is now purely a historical software-engineering milestone
Modern 4D and virtually all software today default to four-digit year entry/display, making the two-digit-year ambiguity this note addresses largely a non-issue in contemporary interfaces

The Sys date format command and SET DATE FORMAT command referenced still exist in modern 4D for locale-aware date formatting, though the specific Y2K-era motivation for using them here is no longer applicable
